method: Whole-file manual reading of KeyboardSimulator and VirtualKey; exact-commit bytes matched Git blob inventory. No key/input APIs executed.
findings: VirtualKey explicitly uses ushort, resolving v14 uncertainty about KEYBDINPUT wVk width. Whole INPUT ABI layout still requires architecture/runtime checks.

Modifier strokes build down events then reverse-order releases; params main-key overload holds all main keys simultaneously, whereas SendKeyPress(params) emits sequential press pairs. These are distinct semantics.

SendInputs returns silently for empty arrays and defaults throwOnError=false; partial native input insertion is ignored in default path. Even throwing path does not compensate for already inserted down events.
CreateKeyDown/Up maps scan byte via MapVirtualKey and sets extended flag for fixed key set; scan-code flag is not set. Keyboard layout-specific behavior and special keys not qualified.

ModifierKeys is public readonly array: reference immutable but elements mutable. Currently-pressed modifier helpers sample key state at separate times and do not preserve one atomic keyboard-state snapshot.

Event-array length arithmetic uses int multiply/add without explicit checked admission, and null arrays are not guarded. CreateKeyInput accepts uint extra-info though structure is native-width; wider tag values cannot be expressed through this helper.
limits: No keyboard simulation, hooks, foreground changes, Windows API execution or original runtime tests. No foreign production code adopted.
